questions.stem: The RBI Governor's call for States to pursue prudent borrowing draws attention to the constitutional and institutional framework governing State debt. Consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Under Article 293 of the Constitution, a State government already indebted to the Union must obtain the Union's consent before raising further loans.
The Fifteenth Finance Commission permits every State to breach the fiscal deficit ceiling of 3% of GSDP without any conditions attached.
State Development Loans (SDLs) are securities issued by State governments and allotted through auctions conducted by the Reserve Bank of India as their debt manager.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct per Article 293(3). Statement 3 is correct — SDLs are State liabilities, with RBI acting only as issuing/debt manager, not as an RBI obligation. Statement 2 is wrong: the extra borrowing space beyond 3% recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission was conditional on power-sector reforms, not unconditional.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra urges states to ensure quality spending, prudent borrowing
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 293 and fiscal federalism/FRBM norms; similar to UPSC 2022 question on fiscal deficit and public debt of state governments.

questions.stem: CBIC's simplification of GST registration is a reminder of the GST architecture. Consider the following pairs:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Levied by the Union government on intra-State supply of goods and services
Levied by State governments on inter-State supply of goods and services
A constitutional body under Article 279A, chaired by the Union Home Minister
Allows small taxpayers to pay GST at a fixed, lower rate without claiming input tax credit
questions.explanation: Pairs 1 and 4 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is wrong because IGST on inter-State supply is levied by the Union government, not the States. Pair 3 is wrong because the GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, not the Union Home Minister.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: GST registration gets easier as CBIC drops Udyam proof, sets seven-day limit for approvals
questions.pyqLink: Tests GST architecture under the 101st Amendment and Article 279A; similar to UPSC 2017/2018 questions on GST Council composition.

questions.stem: With reference to the rejection of the patent application for the BPaL regimen for drug-resistant tuberculosis, consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: The Indian Patent Office rejected the patent application covering the combination of bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid for drug-resistant tuberculosis.

Statement-II: Under Section 3(d) of the Patents Act, 1970, a new form of a known substance is non-patentable unless it demonstrates significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy over the known substance.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct — the patent office rejected the application. Statement-II correctly states the efficacy test under Section 3(d), but it is not the ground on which this specific application was rejected; the opponents' case rested on prior disclosure of the combination in scientific literature and clinical trials since 2015, i.e., lack of inventive step/anticipation, not failure of the efficacy test.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: India rejects patent bid for treatment of drug-resistant TB
questions.pyqLink: Tests patentability criteria under the Patents Act, 1970 (Section 3(d), pre-grant opposition); similar in spirit to UPSC questions on TRIPS and compulsory licensing.

questions.stem: The NPPA's revision of anti-cancer drug prices highlights India's pharmaceutical price control regime. Consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority functions under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.
The Drugs (Prices Control) Order is notified under powers conferred by the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
NPPA's Trade Margin Rationalisation mechanism caps the margin between the price charged to stockists and the Maximum Retail Price, and has been invoked for non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs.
NPPA fixes ceiling prices for all patented drugs sold in India irrespective of whether they are included in the National List of Essential Medicines.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct and consistent with how NPPA and DPCO operate, including the Trade Margin Rationalisation route used for the 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs. Statement 4 is wrong — NPPA's ceiling-price fixation under DPCO applies to scheduled (NLEM) drugs, while patented drugs are generally exempt from direct price-ceiling fixation for a defined period.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Sharp cuts in price of cancer drugs expose excessive pricing, say health experts
questions.pyqLink: Tests drug price control institutional mechanism (NPPA, DPCO, Essential Commodities Act); similar to UPSC 2015 question on National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority's mandate.

questions.stem: A new study on salt marshes softening storm waves draws attention to this coastal ecosystem. Consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Salt marshes are intertidal coastal wetlands dominated by salt-tolerant vegetation that are periodically flooded by tidal action.
Gujarat has India's largest extent of coastal salt marshes, with smaller areas found in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra.
Salt marsh vegetation dissipates wave energy and thereby buffers coastlines against storm surges.
Like mangroves, salt marshes are recognised as blue carbon ecosystems capable of sequestering carbon in their soils.
questions.explanation: All four statements are factually accurate: salt marshes are tidal, vegetated coastal wetlands, with Gujarat holding India's largest share; their vegetation breaks wave energy as shown by flume studies cited in the article, and they are established blue carbon ecosystems alongside mangroves and seagrass meadows.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: How the humble salt marsh softens the ocean’s fury
questions.pyqLink: Tests coastal wetland ecology and blue carbon ecosystems; similar to UPSC 2023 questions on blue carbon and coastal/wetland ecosystems.

questions.stem: With reference to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls reported from Telangana, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls is conducted by the Election Commission of India under its powers derived from the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and Article 324 of the Constitution.
Under the Registration of Electors Rules, Form 6 is used by an elector to apply for deletion of another person's name from the electoral roll.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the ECI's superintendence over electoral rolls flows from Article 324 and the Representation of the People Act, 1950. Statement 2 is wrong: Form 6 is used for new voter registration/inclusion of one's own name, while Form 7 is used to object to an existing entry or seek deletion of another elector's name, as reflected in the article's distinction between Form-6 rejections and Form-7 deletions.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Telangana SIR: Form-6 rejections and Form-7 deletions unusually high during pre-SIR period
questions.pyqLink: Tests Election Commission's constitutional/statutory powers and electoral roll forms; similar to UPSC questions on the Representation of the People Acts.

questions.stem: With reference to coastal ecosystems such as those found along Gujarat's coast, which one of the following best describes a 'salt marsh'?
options: An intertidal wetland dominated by halophytic grasses and herbs that forms along low-energy coastlines and estuaries, distinct from mangrove forests which are dominated by woody halophytic trees.
A permanently submerged offshore ecosystem of calcium carbonate structures built by colonial marine invertebrates.
A low-lying, periodically inundated mudflat found only at river mouths, formed purely by sediment deposition and lacking any vegetation cover.
A hypersaline depression formed by the evaporation of an inland sea, characterised by a crust of salt and seasonal flooding by monsoon runoff.
questions.explanation: Option (a) correctly captures the defining feature of salt marshes — herbaceous halophytic vegetation on tidally flooded, low-energy coasts — distinguishing them from woody mangroves. Option (b) describes a coral reef, option (c) describes an unvegetated tidal mudflat, and option (d) describes a salt pan such as the Rann of Kutch, a near-miss distractor given the Gujarat setting.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: How the humble salt marsh softens the ocean’s fury
questions.pyqLink: Tests classification of coastal landforms/ecosystems (salt marsh vs mangrove vs mudflat vs salt pan); similar to UPSC questions distinguishing coastal and wetland landforms.

questions.stem: The recent Maharashtra Legislative Council (graduates' and teachers' constituencies) elections bring the composition of the Vidhan Parishad into focus. Consider the following statements regarding the Legislative Council:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Legislative Council is a permanent House and, unlike the Legislative Assembly, is not subject to dissolution.
Members representing a teachers' constituency are elected by persons who have been teaching in educational institutions within the State for at least three years.
A Legislative Council can be abolished only after Parliament passes a law to that effect, following a resolution passed by the State Legislative Assembly by a special majority.
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Like the Rajya Sabha, the Vidhan Parishad is a continuing chamber with one-third of members retiring every two years (Statement 1). Article 171(3)(c) requires teachers' constituency electors to have taught for at least three years in institutions not lower than secondary school (Statement 2). Article 169 requires the State Assembly to first pass a special-majority resolution before Parliament can legislate to create or abolish a Council (Statement 3).
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Maharashtra MLC election: Congress trumps BJP in Nagpur, MVA leads 3-2 in State
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 171 composition of Legislative Councils and Article 169 procedure for their creation/abolition, similar to UPSC 2017 question on the Rajya Sabha/Vidhan Parishad's permanent character.

questions.stem: With reference to the rupee's exchange rate and India's external sector, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Reserve Bank of India intervenes in the foreign exchange market mainly to curb excessive volatility in the rupee's exchange rate, not to defend a fixed target.
India's foreign exchange reserves consist only of foreign currency assets and do not include the country's gold holdings.
A depreciation of the rupee tends to make imports costlier while improving the price competitiveness of India's exports.
India currently follows a fixed exchange rate regime under which the RBI commits to maintaining the rupee at a set value against the US dollar.
questions.explanation: Only statements 1 and 3 are correct. India follows a market-determined (managed float) exchange rate, so the RBI smooths volatility rather than defending a fixed rate, making statement 4 false. Reserves comprise Foreign Currency Assets, gold, SDRs and the Reserve Tranche Position with the IMF, so statement 2 is false since it excludes gold.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Rupee rises 11 paise to 95.17 against U.S. dollar in early trade
questions.pyqLink: Tests composition of forex reserves and India's exchange rate regime, a recurring theme in UPSC questions on RBI's external sector operations.

questions.stem: Jio Platforms' stock market debut was widely reported in terms of its 'market capitalisation'. With reference to the Indian stock market, which one of the following best describes the term 'market capitalisation' of a listed company?
options: It is the total value of a company's assets as recorded in its balance sheet, also known as its book value.
It is the price at which a company's shares are first offered to the public during an Initial Public Offering.
It is the market value of only those shares that are readily available for trading, excluding promoter holdings.
It is the current market price of a company's share multiplied by the total number of its outstanding shares.
questions.explanation: Market capitalisation equals current share price multiplied by total outstanding shares, which is how Jio Platforms' and Reliance Industries' valuations were computed and compared in the news. Option (a) describes book value, not market value; option (b) describes the issue price at IPO; option (c) describes 'free-float' market capitalisation, a narrower related but distinct concept.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Jio becomes India’s second-most valuable company: How its listing pushed Reliance past Tatas, Adanis
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static concept of market capitalisation versus book value/free-float, similar in style to UPSC 2019's 'Merchant Discount Rate' best-describes question.

questions.stem:
Consider the following two statements regarding the rapid intensification of Cyclone Arnab before its landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast:
Statement-I: Cyclone Arnab intensified from a low-pressure system into a very severe cyclonic storm within a few days, with its landfall occurring earlier than initially forecast.
Statement-II: El Niño, characterised by abnormal warming of the Pacific Ocean's surface waters, can alter atmospheric conditions over the Bay of Bengal in ways that favour faster intensification of tropical cyclones.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is factually correct — Arnab intensified rapidly and made landfall ahead of the IMD's original forecast. Statement-II is also correct and explanatory: El Niño is an ENSO-related ocean-atmosphere phenomenon that modifies sea surface temperature and wind shear patterns over the Indian Ocean basin, which the news report explicitly linked to Arnab's rapid intensification and faster movement.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: How El Niño made Cyclone Arnab stronger and faster
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static concept of El Niño/ENSO and ocean-atmosphere interaction affecting cyclogenesis, an Environment & Ecology staple since UPSC 2022-23 introduced the Statement-I/II format.

questions.stem: A study involving Parkinson's patients in Keralam examined the link between gut bacteria and the disease. Consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Parkinson's disease is caused by the progressive loss of dopamine-producing nerve cells in the brain.
The 'gut-brain axis' refers to the bidirectional biochemical communication between the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system.
16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing is a technique used to identify the bacteria present in a sample based on their genetic material.
Non-motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease, such as constipation, typically appear only after the onset of motor symptoms like tremors.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct and describe established concepts underlying the study. Statement 4 is false and reverses the actual finding: the article notes that non-motor symptoms like constipation can appear years before motor symptoms such as tremors begin, not after.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Study in Keralam sheds light on link between gut bacteria, Parkinson’s disease
questions.pyqLink: Tests understanding of the gut-brain axis and basic genomic sequencing techniques, concepts tested in UPSC's biotechnology and human physiology questions.

questions.stem: Kozhikode recently marked three years since becoming India's first UNESCO 'City of Literature'. Consider the following pairs of Indian cities and the category under which they have been designated in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Only Kozhikode (Literature) and Jaipur (Crafts and Folk Art) are correctly matched. Hyderabad is designated under 'Gastronomy', not Crafts and Folk Art; Chennai is designated under 'Music', while Mumbai holds the 'Film' designation.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: As Kozhikode marks three years of ‘City of Literature’ recognition, writers seek more focus at local level
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's UNESCO Creative Cities Network designations, in the style of UPSC 2023's 'correctly matched pairs' questions on places/regions in the news.

questions.stem:
With reference to tropical cyclones in the North Indian Ocean, as illustrated by Cyclone Arnab, consider the following statements:
1. The India Meteorological Department classifies a cyclonic disturbance as a 'Very Severe Cyclonic Storm' when its associated maximum sustained surface wind speed is between 118 kmph and 165 kmph.
2. Tropical cyclones forming in the North Indian Ocean are named exclusively by the coastal country within whose maritime zone the system develops, with Bay of Bengal systems named by India and Arabian Sea systems named by Pakistan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 correctly reflects the IMD's wind-speed based classification scale, where 118-165 kmph corresponds to a 'Very Severe Cyclonic Storm' (consistent with Arnab's reported 125-135 kmph winds). Statement 2 is incorrect: cyclone names are drawn from a common rotational list contributed by all 13 member countries of the WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones, applied regardless of whether the system forms in the Bay of Bengal or the Arabian Sea.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Cyclone Arnab to weaken into depression on October 29, says IMD | LIVE updates
questions.pyqLink: Tests IMD's cyclone intensity classification scale and the regional cyclone-naming convention, a recurring Indian Physical Geography/disaster topic.

questions.stem: A special MP-MLA court recently acquitted a politician in a criminal defamation case. Consider the following statements regarding the law of criminal defamation in India. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Defamation in India is actionable both as a civil wrong (tort) and as a criminal offence.
A criminal defamation complaint can generally be filed only by the person who claims to be aggrieved by the statement, subject to certain statutory exceptions.
Truth is a complete defence to a charge of criminal defamation under all circumstances.
Special MP-MLA courts have jurisdiction restricted only to offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: defamation is both a tort and an offence under criminal law, and Section 199 CrPC restricts criminal defamation complaints to the 'aggrieved person' (with limited exceptions). Statement 3 is wrong — under Exception 1 to Section 499 IPC, truth is a defence only if the imputation was made for the public good, not unconditionally. Statement 4 is wrong — MP-MLA courts were constituted on Supreme Court directions to fast-track all pending criminal cases against sitting/former legislators, not just PC Act cases.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Why special MP-MLA court acquitted Rahul Gandhi of criminal defamation
questions.pyqLink: Tests Section 499/500 IPC defamation law and Section 199 CrPC complaint procedure; similar to UPSC's recurring focus on reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2).

questions.stem: The Union government recently hiked Dearness Allowance (DA) for central government employees. With reference to DA, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Dearness Allowance for central government employees is calculated using the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) compiled by the Labour Bureau.
Dearness Allowance is revised only once in a financial year, with effect from 1st April.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — DA/DR revisions are based on the 12-monthly average of CPI-IW released by the Labour Bureau. Statement 2 is incorrect — DA is generally revised twice a year, typically with effect from 1 January and 1 July, not once from 1 April.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: DA hike: How is DA calculated, what hike means for employees, exchequer
questions.pyqLink: Tests the CPI-IW basis of Dearness Allowance, a recurring static-economy concept linked to inflation indexation of wages.

questions.stem: Cyclone Arnab recently made landfall on India's east coast. With reference to the naming of tropical cyclones in the North Indian Ocean, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: A tropical cyclone in the North Indian Ocean is assigned a name only after its maximum sustained surface wind speed reaches at least 34 knots (about 62 km/h).
A cyclone's name must correspond to the country over whose territorial waters the storm first originates.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — naming happens only once a system crosses the cyclonic-storm wind-speed threshold of 34 knots. Statement 2 is incorrect — names are drawn in sequence from a common regional list contributed by North Indian Ocean countries, irrespective of where the cyclone actually originates or makes landfall.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Arnab smashes into the east coast: How cyclones are named
questions.pyqLink: Tests the IMD-RSMC cyclone naming convention for the North Indian Ocean, a recurring Geography/Disaster Management PYQ theme.

questions.stem: Deutsche Bank expects the RBI to tighten monetary policy over the coming months. With reference to the RBI's monetary policy framework, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against the collateral of government securities.
The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the RBI has six members, and the RBI Governor has a casting vote in the event of a tie.
Under the flexible inflation targeting framework, the RBI is mandated to maintain CPI inflation at 4%, with a tolerance band of plus or minus 4 percentage points.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — repo operations are collateralised lending against government securities, and the six-member MPC gives the Governor a casting vote on a tie. Statement 3 is incorrect — the statutory tolerance band around the 4% CPI inflation target is plus or minus 2 percentage points, not 4.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: RBI may hike repo rate to 6.25% by H1 2027, warns Deutsche Bank as inflation risks persist
questions.pyqLink: Tests the composition of the Monetary Policy Committee and the inflation-targeting band, both frequently asked static Economy concepts.

questions.stem: A case involving a minor driver in Kochi has drawn attention to liability provisions under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. Consider the following pairs of provisions and the offence/liability they relate to. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Driving in violation of the prescribed age requirement
Fixes culpability on the traffic police officer concerned
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched as per the Motor Vehicles Act. Pair 4 is incorrect — Section 199A, inserted by the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, fixes culpability on the guardian or owner of the vehicle driven by a juvenile offender, not on any traffic police officer.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Kochi road rage case: When are parents liable for driving offences by minors?
questions.pyqLink: Tests specific sections of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988/2019 amendment on juvenile driving liability — institutional/statutory detail UPSC favours.

questions.stem: NCRB data shows Punjab leading the country in drug trafficking cases. With reference to the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, which one of the following best describes the term 'commercial quantity'?
options: The quantity of a narcotic drug or psychotropic substance above which the Act prescribes a rigorous imprisonment of ten to twenty years, with the threshold specified separately for each drug.
The total quantity of drugs seized across a state in a calendar year, as compiled by the National Crime Records Bureau for trafficking statistics.
The quantity of a drug that a licensed pharmaceutical company may legally possess for industrial manufacturing purposes.
The minimum quantity of drug seizure required to classify a case as inter-state trafficking under the Act.
questions.explanation: Under the NDPS Act, offences are graded by quantity — small quantity, quantity lesser than commercial (intermediate), and commercial quantity — with commercial quantity attracting the most severe punishment (10 to 20 years' rigorous imprisonment plus fine), the threshold notified separately for each substance. The other options describe NCRB reporting practice or unrelated licensing/jurisdictional concepts, not the statutory term.
questions.subject: Social Issues & Schemes
questions.sourceTitle: Why Punjab can't shake off drug crisis: Role of history, geography, economics
questions.pyqLink: Tests the quantity-based sentencing structure of the NDPS Act, 1985, a recurring static concept behind drug-trafficking news.
